answer:
Originally, the plan was to work 20 hours per week for 12 weeks, totaling \(20 \times 12 = 240\) hours. This would earn \$3000, giving an hourly rate of \(\frac{3000}{240} = 12.50\) dollars per hour.

Due to being sick for the first two weeks, there are \(12 - 2 = 10\) weeks left to work. The total amount needed is still \$3000, which requires the same 240 hours of work. 

To find the new weekly hours needed:
\[
\text{Hours per week} = \frac{240 \text{ hours}}{10 \text{ weeks}} = 24 \text{ hours/week}
\]

Verifying with the hourly rate:
\[
\text{Weekly earnings needed} = \frac{3000}{10} = 300 \text{ dollars/week}
\]
\[
\text{Hours per week} = \frac{300}{12.50} = 24 \text{ hours/week}
\]

Both methods confirm that the required hours per week are \(\boxed{24}\).
